'''Mónica Kräuter''' (born 18 September 1967) is a Venezuelan chemist and professor of the [[Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)|Simón Bolívar University]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ceipusb.weebly.com/conociendolasimoacuten/3ra-edicion-conociendo-a-la-prof-monica-krauter|title=3ra Edición: ¡Conociendo a la Prof. Mónica Krauter!|date=26 December 2015|access-date=1 November 2017|agency=CEIP USB|language=es-ES}}</ref> She gained notability during the [[2017 Venezuelan protests]] due to her study of [[tear gas]] canisters and her advice on how to protect against its effects.

==Career==
Mónica Kräuter graduated as a chemist from [[Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)|Simón Bolívar University]] in 1993, and she obtained a master's degree in chemistry with an environment specialty in 2000 at Simón Bolívar University as well.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://verdelatierra.com/la-cientifica-monica-krauter-explica-que-son-las-bombas-lacrimogenas-y-que-efectos-tienen-sobre-la-salud/|title=La científica Mónica Krauter explica qué son las bombas lacrimógenas y qué efectos tienen sobre la salud|date=20 May 2017|work=Verde la Tierra|access-date=1 November 2017|language=es-ES}}</ref> She has been a professor of the university in the systems and processes department since her graduation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://usbnoticias.info/post/51709|title=Mónica Krauter: "La represión es cada vez más cruel"|last=Pilato|first=Elsa|date=20 June 2017|work=USBnoticias|access-date=1 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107013300/https://usbnoticias.info/post/51709|archive-date=7 November 2017|url-status=dead|language=es-ES}}</ref>

She carried out a study that involved the collection of thousands of tear gas canisters fired by Venezuelan authorities in 2014. She stated that the majority of canisters used the main component [[CS gas]], supplied by Cóndor of Brazil, which meets [[Geneva Conventions|Geneva Convention]] requirements, but that 72% of the tear gas used was expired and other canisters produced in Venezuela by [[CAVIM|Cavim]] did not show adequate labels or expiration dates. Following the expiration of tear gas, she notes that it "breaks down into [[cyanide]] oxide, [[phosgene]]s and [[nitrogen]]s that are extremely dangerous".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lapatilla.com/site/2017/04/08/bombas-lacrimogenas-que-usa-el-gobierno-estan-vencidas-y-emanan-cianuro-recomendaciones/|title=Bombas lacrimógenas que usa el gobierno están vencidas y emanan cianuro (+ recomendaciones)|date=8 April 2017|work=[[La Patilla]]|access-date=9 April 2017|language=es-ES|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410051345/https://www.lapatilla.com/site/2017/04/08/bombas-lacrimogenas-que-usa-el-gobierno-estan-vencidas-y-emanan-cianuro-recomendaciones|archive-date=10 April 2017}}</ref> Kräuter has advised against the use of [[vinegar]] to neutralize the effects of tear gas since it is an [[acid]], instead recommending the use of [[sodium bicarbonate]] or [[antacids]] such as [[Maalox]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://tururutururu.com/prof-usb-monica-krauter-como-reaccionar-ante-las-bombas-lacrimogenas/|title=Prof USB Mónica Kräuter, Cómo reaccionar ante las bombas lacrimógenas|date=26 May 2017|work=Tururutururu|access-date=1 November 2017|language=es-ES|archive-date=7 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107025513/http://tururutururu.com/prof-usb-monica-krauter-como-reaccionar-ante-las-bombas-lacrimogenas/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2018 she was listed by [[Americas Quarterly]] as one of the ''10 People Who Will (One Day) Rebuild Venezuela.''<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.americasquarterly.org/content/educator-monica-krauter|title=10 People Who Will (One Day) Rebuild Venezuela: The Educator|last=Krygier|first=Rachelle|work=Americas Quarterly|access-date=3 June 2018|first2=Mariana|last2=Zúñiga}}</ref>
